structured_output.world_model: W2 (empirical), after E025. Tip is E023: 6.198 s, 0.7538 (9.0 true epochs). Measured regularities: the epoch dial is worth about 0.1-0.15 pp and about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, and it is roughly linear. Resolution cuts are the most expensive in accuracy. wd, label smoothing, Muon lr and EMA-shape tweaks are flat within noise (E009, E013, E014, E022, E025). The 3-seed noise is ±0.3 pp. Time is predictable from FLOPs and pixel count. E023 landed at 0.7538 with seeds re-rolled, so every further trim sits at or just below the 0.753 bar.

forecasts.reason: A further 0.25-0.5 epoch trim costs about 0.1 pp from a base already only 0.05 pp above the bar, so it is a coin flip that probably lands under 0.753.
The saving is real but smaller than the back-of-envelope, because BN/GELU and graph overhead remain. Accuracy loss is probably small but unreadable at this noise level.
Dropping 10% of samples is about the same as cutting steps. Hard-example focus is unlikely to give a measurable gain, and the loss buffer adds a little overhead.
The time gain is small because the step is compute-bound, about 1.5%. Fewer steps cost a little accuracy.
Muon lr has been flat within noise (E014 +0.09 pp), so the expected effect is zero ± 0.3 pp at unchanged time.

cruxes: What is the held-out seeds 3-12 mean of E023? If it is at or above 0.7535, a trim is affordable. If it is below, any trim fails.
Does the backward truncation in I043 actually save 4% or more of time under CUDA graphs?
Is a gain of 0.15 pp or more from any accuracy lever (I038/I046) real on held-out seeds, rather than 3-seed noise?
